market_summary: Singapore banks are the dominant story: the Fed's Sept 16 hike lifted net interest margin expectations and Jefferies initiated coverage with Buy on DBS/UOB (Hold on OCBC) on Sept 22-23, reinforcing the STI's 24.6% YTD run. Institutional flows into SGX names are reversing course, with Keppel and Thai Beverage flipping from H1 outflows to Q3 inflows (per Sept 25 report), while SGX Group itself posted record FY2026 volumes and got a fresh price-target hike (Sept 27). On the US side, Big Tech earnings were mixed against lofty AI-spending expectations, and Meta's sharp one-day drop (-3.3%) after a huge 30%+ one-month run suggests some profit-taking/de-rating risk in the most extended AI trades. Overall risk appetite for SGX equities looks constructive and catalyst-driven, while US mega-cap tech looks stretched on some names and more balanced on others.

picks.thesis: DBS is the largest STI weight and just received a fresh Buy initiation from Jefferies alongside the Fed's Sept 16 hike, which directly expands bank net interest margins. Price is up 2.7% vs its 50-day MA and only 0.8% off its 52-week high, showing the market is already rewarding the rate tailwind, and further margin/dividend compounding could extend the move over the next few months.
picks.news: Jefferies initiated coverage with Buy on DBS (Sept 22, 2026); Fed hiked rates 25bp Sept 16, 2026, directly benefiting Singapore bank margins, with DBS/OCBC/UOB comprising 40-54% of STI weight.
picks.risks: Implied upside from consensus target is only ~0.2%, meaning much of the good news may already be priced in; any dovish Fed pivot or credit-quality scare in Singapore banks would remove the core rate-margin thesis.

picks.thesis: Keppel just posted a sharp institutional flow reversal - S$159.2m of net inflows in Q3 versus a S$35.7m outflow in H1 - a concrete, dated signal that big money is rotating back in. Analysts are heavily bullish (12 buy/1 hold/2 sell) with 12.9% implied upside to consensus target, and the stock has been flat/range-bound (vs MA200 -0.1%) rather than overextended, leaving room to re-rate on the improving flow picture.
picks.news: Q3 2026 institutional inflow report (Sept 25, 2026): Keppel recorded S$159.2m net inflows, reversing a S$35.7m H1 outflow.
picks.risks: A single quarter of institutional buying can reverse quickly; if flows stall or broader SGX sentiment cools, the stock could revert to its prior 6-month softness (-5% over 6m).

picks.thesis: UOB received a Buy initiation from Jefferies alongside DBS on the same Fed-hike margin thesis, but the stock has lagged DBS/OCBC's rally (only +6.7% 3m vs OCBC's +28.7%), leaving more room to catch up. It also sits 5.3% off its 52-week high, giving a better entry point than the other two banks.
picks.news: Jefferies initiated Buy on UOB (Sept 22, 2026), citing scope for earnings/dividend compounding from the Fed's Sept 16 rate hike.
picks.risks: Analyst consensus is more cautious overall (3 buy/11 hold/2 sell), suggesting the Street sees UOB as fairly valued; underperformance versus peers could persist if the market keeps favoring DBS/OCBC.

picks.thesis: SGX just reported record FY2026 volumes (securities turnover +35% y/y, derivatives +15% y/y, highest daily securities value in 18 years) and analysts raised the price target to S$24.15 from S$22.33 on Sept 27 - both fresh, fundamentally positive catalysts. The stock has pulled back 11.4% over the past month and sits 7.5% below its 50-day MA, so the price has not yet caught up to the improving operating and analyst-target trend, offering a valuation gap to close.
picks.news: SGX Group FY2026 record trading volumes report; price target raised to S$24.15 from S$22.33 (Sept 27, 2026).
picks.risks: The recent price weakness could reflect a real negative not captured in this news (e.g., cost pressure, one-off items, market-wide de-rating of exchanges); if the downtrend (-7.5% vs MA50) continues, the fundamental story alone may not be enough to turn price around quickly.

picks.thesis: Meta fell 3.3% on the day after an enormous run-up (+30.5% in one month, +22.1% above its 50-day MA), making it the most extended of the mega-cap AI names against a backdrop of mixed AI-spending sentiment following recent Big Tech earnings. The scale of the pullback after such a steep rally suggests profit-taking or a negative reassessment is underway, and a name this stretched is vulnerable to further mean reversion over the coming days to weeks.
picks.news: Big Tech earnings (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet) showed mixed results relative to elevated AI-spending expectations; Meta's stock dropped -3.3% intraday against this backdrop.
picks.risks: Analyst sentiment remains overwhelmingly bullish (55 buy/7 hold/0 sell) with 5.1% further upside to target, so this is a tactical, momentum-driven short, not a fundamental one; a single strong data point (e.g., ad-revenue beat) could quickly reverse the drop.

picks.thesis: OCBC has had the strongest 1-year run of the three Singapore banks (+96.9%) yet Jefferies only gave it a Hold (versus Buy on DBS/UOB) on Sept 22, and consensus analyst target implies a slight -1.5% downside from current levels - a rare negative-implied-upside reading in this rally. This suggests OCBC's valuation has run ahead of its relative fundamentals within the sector, making it the weakest of the three banks on a forward basis.
picks.news: Jefferies initiated OCBC with a Hold rating (vs Buy on DBS/UOB) on Sept 22-23, 2026, even as the broader bank sector benefits from the Sept 16 Fed hike.
picks.risks: OCBC is still riding the same sector-wide margin tailwind as DBS/UOB, and its momentum (+3.6% 1m, +48.4% 6m) has been the strongest of the trio, so it could keep grinding higher purely on sector sentiment despite the softer analyst rating.
